title: June Pike's talk needs expected_snapshot_hash and nothing says so until the call fails
body:
## The call, and the exact rejection

One contact in the game requires an argument no other contact requires, and nothing says so until
the call has already failed.

    tool  : mcp__adventureforge__talk_overworld_session_contact
    args  : {"session_id": "...", "character_id": "albany_city__transport_hub__june_pike"}
    error : "To talk to June here, pass expected_snapshot_hash from the revealed Station board."

That rejection is byte-identical in every occurrence I sampled, across seeds 1788650589,
1788651590, 1788653558, 1788653559, 1788655559 and 1788666347 — spanning builds 2da50f33 through
2a9d6817.

**What the player expected**: `talk_overworld_session_contact` to behave as it does for every other
contact in the game, which is `session_id` + `character_id` and no guard argument. Players reach
June Pike after revealing the Station board, call talk exactly as they have called it a dozen times
already, and are refused.

**What happens next** (seed 1788650589, consecutive calls on the same contact):

    0: talk_overworld_session_contact  hash_passed=False  ok=False
       err: To talk to June here, pass expected_snapshot_hash from the revealed Station board.
    1: talk_overworld_session_contact  hash_passed=True   ok=True
    2: step_action                     ok=True

So the rejection IS recoverable in one retry, and the message is what makes it recoverable. That is
the reason this is P1 and not P0 — nobody is blocked. It is also the reason it keeps being reported:
every player pays the same avoidable failed call, and several describe it as the moment the game
stopped feeling like a game and started feeling like an API.

## One correction to what the tickets say

Two clusters describe the tool as "rejecting the current snapshot hash and requiring the hash from a
separate prior reveal call". **The engine never does that.** I searched every retained transcript for
a rejection where `expected_snapshot_hash` WAS supplied and found zero. Every failure in the corpus
is the argument being absent. The "rejected my hash" phrasing is the player's inference about why
they were refused, not observed behaviour — worth knowing before anyone goes looking for a
hash-comparison bug that is not there.

## Counts per bucket, with ticket ids

| ticket_id | n | severity | kind | as the players worded it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `36eab840c6701985` | 9 | S1 | experience | "June Pike talk required an undocumented snapshot hash after Station board reveal" |
| `344de27fec554eeb` | 4 | S2 | bug | "Ally talk action rejected the current snapshot hash and required the hash from a separate prior reveal call" |
| `77fb87f37aee0631` | 3 | S1 | experience | "June Pike dialogue required an undisclosed expected_snapshot_hash on first attempt" |
| `29cbd45a41e6e349` | 2 | S1 | experience | "Parallel tool calls against sequential embedded-quest state produce stale-hash rejections" |
| `3a34440102590875` | 2 | S0 | bug | "Rejected on first attempt for a missing expected_snapshot_hash… error message named the fix and retry succeeded" |

**20 reports of one defect**, split across five ticket identities because triage keys on wording.
All five are `promotion: accumulating` and none can promote: this fleet is single-vendor, so
`derivePromotion` cannot return `corroborated` for any of them (see
`ops/patches/promotion-single-lineage.note.md`). That is why this arrives as a submission rather
than through the bucket.

## Builds it spans — this is not fixed

First seen `2da50f33`, last seen `2a9d6817`, continuously present in between (`73a02866`,
`9230ce5e`, `2ba18c67`, `5afc7531` all carry occurrences). Nine builds, one month of the corpus, no
change in the rejection text or the failure rate.

## Fix shape, in observable terms

Any ONE of these makes the finding stop recurring, in rough order of how much it changes:

1. **Signal the requirement before the call.** The contact's listing already reaches the player;
   if it carried the guard requirement the way a job's options are meant to, the player would pass
   the argument on the first attempt and no failed call would happen. Observable test: a player who
   reads the contact listing and then calls talk succeeds without a retry.
2. **Accept the call and return the guard value.** If the reveal already established the state, the
   tool could accept `session_id` + `character_id` and answer with the hash it wants echoed rather
   than refusing. Observable test: the first talk call on June Pike returns `ok: true`.
3. **Keep refusing, but make the refusal self-contained.** The current message names the argument
   and where it comes from, which is why recovery works — but it does not give the value. Naming
   the exact hash in the rejection would make the retry mechanical. Observable test: the rejection
   contains the value the next call must pass.

Option 1 is the one players ask for in their own words; option 3 is the smallest.

## Evidence

- Store `/home/user/adventureforge-playtest/sessions`, 44 completed sessions, all `runner_enforced`.
- Retained client transcripts under `ai-runs/playtest/runs/*.claude-session.jsonl` for the seeds
  named above; the call/response sequences quoted here are reproducible from them.

---

## ADDENDUM (2026-09-07, wave 6 on build 2a9d6817) — the root cause is sharper than "unsignalled"

Report 21 of this family states the defect better than the twenty before it, and I verified the
claim against the schema:

> "talk_overworld_session_contact rejected without expected_snapshot_hash, though the schema
> describes that field as an **optional staleness guard**." — session
> `20260907T004409Z…70dc8fe51ef0`, S1

That is exactly what the schema says (`src/mcp/server.ts`, `EXPECTED_SNAPSHOT_HASH`):

    expected_snapshot_hash: z.string().optional()
      .describe("Reject the action if this snapshot hash is stale.")

So the declared contract is: *optional; supply it and I will refuse a stale action.* The runtime
contract is: *sometimes mandatory, and the action is refused without it.* **Players are not failing
to read the tool description — they are following it.** That reframes the whole family from a
signposting problem to a contract violation.

Second fact from the same wave, and it explains why this reads as capricious rather than as a rule:
the requirement is CONDITIONAL, not per-contact. In seed 1788727014 the first `june_pike` talk
**succeeded with no hash**; in seed 1788727013 the first talk was **refused** without one. Same
contact, same build, opposite outcomes — the difference is whether the Station board had been
revealed. A player therefore learns "this call works", uses it again, and is refused.

This narrows the fix. Option 3 in the list above (make the rejection self-contained) treats a symptom.
The contract-level fixes are the real candidates:

1. **Make the description tell the truth about conditionality** — cheapest, and it would have
   prevented all 21 reports: say that the field becomes required once a Station reveal is pending.
2. **Do not make an optional field conditionally mandatory.** If the guard is required after a
   reveal, that is a distinct precondition and belongs in the reveal's own contract, not in an
   argument documented as optional.

Observable test for either: a player who reads the tool schema, reveals the Station board, and then
talks to June Pike either succeeds, or is refused by something the schema warned them about.


## Acceptance for the contract fix (added 2026-09-07)

1. **The schema description and the runtime agree.** Either the description of
   `expected_snapshot_hash` states exactly WHEN the hash is required and WHERE it comes from, or the
   conditional requirement moves into the reveal's own contract — so that a field documented as
   optional is never, in any state, mandatory. Pick one and say which in the commit message.
2. **The rejection keeps naming the value and its source.** The current wording
   ("To talk to June here, pass expected_snapshot_hash from the revealed Station board.") is the one
   thing this defect already does well: it names the argument and where to get it. Do not lose that
   while fixing the contract.
3. **A regression pins BOTH paths**, because the capriciousness is the defect: the pending-reveal
   path (`exactReadyStationJuneBoard` true) and the no-reveal path (false) are each asserted, so a
   future change cannot make the requirement unconditional or drop it silently. Verified directly in
   `src/mcp/server.ts`: the throw at the June Pike talk sits behind that guard, and the schema
   (`EXPECTED_SNAPSHOT_HASH`) declares `z.string().optional()` described as "Reject the action if
   this snapshot hash is stale." Those two statements are the contradiction to close.

evidence.summary: 20 reports across 5 ticket ids, 44 sessions, 9 builds - the corpus's most corroborated finding. Recoverable in one retry, so P1 not P0; single-vendor fleet means none of the five can ever promote.
